answer_sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
  ON s.store_key = l.store_key
WHERE
  NOT s.close_date IS NULL

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: The one returned value, 3,205,452.33 USD: every dollar Contoso actually charged customers, after discount, on all 2,725 sales lines ever rung up at a shop that has since closed — 1,140 orders placed between 2016-05-18 and 2019-11-02, which is the whole span these shops traded in, with no date window imposed. Sixteen premises qualify as closed and 6 of them produced this money; the other 10 shut between 2015-05-05 and 2016-07-07, at or before the sales record starts, so they belong to the population and contribute nothing. WHAT IS NOT IN THE FIGURE: nothing from the 57 shops still trading, and nothing from the web shop — the online row has no close date, so it is not a closed store, which makes this physical-shop money only and not comparable with an all-channel revenue total. It is net: the same sales at list price come to 3,405,539.83, the 200,087.50 difference being discount. And it is attributed to premises, the grain sales are recorded against, so nothing is double-counted at the one site that was re-let and closed twice.

value.means: Every premises the store dimension records — 74 rows, one per shop per trading period, over 67 distinct sites. Of these, 57 are physical shops with no close date (still trading), 16 are physical premises carrying a close date (9 annotated 'Closed', 7 'Restructured', those 7 standing on only 6 sites because one site was re-let twice), and 1 is the online sentinel (location_code -1), which carries no close date and a null status. Nothing is filtered yet and nothing is measured yet: this is the population the "closed" filter will cut and the revenue sum will be taken over, and it is at PREMISES grain, which is the grain every sale is recorded against via store_key.

turns.why: Four of the first eight closed shops shut before the sales record even begins, so price both open forks in one query: the shut/restructured split inside "closed", and whether any sale at all is recorded AFTER a store's close date — if none is, "all revenue ever" and "revenue up to closing" are the same figure and the second ambiguity dissolves.
turns.did:
SELECT
  s.status_annotation,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.store_key) AS closed_stores,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT l.order_key IS NULL THEN s.store_key END) AS stores_with_sales,
  COUNT(l.order_key) AS sales_lines,
  SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_date > s.close_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS lines_after_close,
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS net_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_date <= s.close_date THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_revenue_up_to_close
FROM contoso_served.dim_store AS s
LEFT JOIN contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  ON l.store_key = s.store_key
WHERE
  NOT s.close_date IS NULL
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  1
